blocks.text: The elder says that he has more to communicate but does not wish to do so with ink and pen. Instead, he hopes to visit Gaius soon so they can speak “mouth to mouth,” meaning face to face. The closing therefore distinguishes the present written message from matters the elder expects to address personally.

The precise literary relationship among these writings is disputed, but 2 John shares a concentrated pattern of vocabulary, formulas, and concerns with 1 John, 3 John, and the Fourth Gospel. This places 3 John within a recognizable cluster of related writings without, by itself, settling questions about how they were composed or connected.
